summary: Ulrike Roesler is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology who earned her PhD from the University of Münster. She taught at Freiburg and Marburg, and later became Professor of Tibetan and Himalayan Studies at Oxford.

Uma Chakravarti is a historian and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Mount Carmel College, Banaras Hindu University, University Law College, and the University of Delhi under D. Devahuti. She taught at Miranda House from 1966 to 1998.

Umakant Premanand Shah was an Indologist and historian. He served as deputy director and head of the Ramayana Project at the Oriental Institute, Vadodara, and was director at the Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda from circa 1964 to 1975.

Umesha Mishra was an Indologist and philosopher who served at the University of Allahabad from circa 1923 to 1959. He was founder secretary of Ganganatha Jha Kendriya Sanskrit Vidyapeetha and director of the Mithila Institute from circa 1951 to 1961.

Unnikrishnan Payyappallimana is an Indologist who studied at Ayurveda College, Coimbatore, and the University of Amsterdam. He held posts at the FRLHT, Amala Institute of Medical Sciences, and served as a visiting associate professor at the University of Toyama.

Unrai Wogihara was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Junjirō Takakusu and Ernst Leumann at the University of Strasbourg. He taught at the University of Tokyo and served as Professor of Sanskrit at Taisho University.
Unsho Shaku was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Mount Koya in 1844. He taught Ekai Kawaguchi and founded Juze-kai, Kairitsu Gakko, and Juuzen Hokutsu.

Uranchimeg B. Ujeed works in Buddhist and Central Asian studies. She completed her PhD at SOAS University of London and served as a Research Associate in the Mongolia and Inner Asia Unit at the University of Cambridge.

Uranchimeg Tsultem is a scholar of Buddhist studies and art history who completed her PhD at UC Berkeley. She has held teaching and research roles at UC Berkeley, the National University of Mongolia, and IUPUI's Herron School of Art and Design.

Uranchimeg Tsultemin is a scholar of art history, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology who earned her PhD from the University of California, Berkeley. She has served as a lecturer at UC Berkeley and as an associate professor at the National University of Mongolia.

Urs App is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology who earned his PhD from Temple University and studied at Kyoto University. He served as Associate Director at Hanazono University and held research posts at the EFEO and ISEAS.
Usha Nilsson was an Indologist and linguist. She served as a faculty member and later Emeritus Professor of Languages and Cultures of Asia at the University of Wisconsin-Madison.
Usharbudh Arya was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of London. He held a post at the University of Minnesota from circa 1967 to 1973.
Uta Reinöhl is a linguist and Indologist. She held a post at the University of Cologne in 2018 and serves as Chair of General Linguistics at the University of Freiburg.

Ute Hüsken is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned her doctorate under Heinz Bechert at Göttingen. She was a professor at the University of Oslo from 2007 to 2017 before becoming a professor at Heidelberg University in 2017.

Utz Podzeit was an Indologist who earned his doctorate from the University of Vienna. He held a research stay at the University of Madras and served as a university lecturer in Indology at the University of Vienna.
V. Kameswari is an Indologist associated with the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute, where she has served as an Editorial Committee member and research supervisor.
Vinayaka P. Bhatta is an Indologist and linguist who has served as head and Professor-Editor of the Sanskrit Dictionary Project at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute.
V. R. Srinivasan is an Indology and religious studies scholar who pursued doctoral research at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute under the supervision of V. Yamuna Devi.

V. Raghavan was an Indologist who earned his PhD from the University of Madras under S. Kuppuswami Sastri. He served on the faculty at the University of Madras and founded the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute, serving as its secretary.
